title: Airfare of the Week: China Southern Business Class Madrid – Brisbane from $4,988 Return
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Brisbane, Australia. Photo: Adobe Stock.
Our newest Airfare of the Week belongs to China Southern Airlines, which has round-trip Business Class fares from Madrid (MAD) to Brisbane (BNE) from EUR3,153 (~AU$4,988).
This is a Europe-originating fare, so it is best suited to travellers who are already in Europe or who want to add a cheap Business Class trip home to Brisbane onto a separate ticket to Spain. With travel available during the Australian summer, it’s a well-timed deal for anyone visiting family or escaping the European winter.
Here are the full details of this great Business Class airfare from Madrid to Brisbane.
Sample itinerary & pricing
Example pricing. Screenshot from Google Flights.
You can book this fare on the China Southern website . Some online travel agents (OTAs) offer this itinerary from $4,669. But, as always, buyer beware.
Flights to Sydney are priced at similar levels.
Note that fares and availability are subject to change. This fare may not be available by the time you read this article, and you might need to be flexible with travel dates. We recommend booking ASAP to avoid disappointment!
Travel dates & fare rules
Here are the details of this airfare:
Book by 31 December 2026
Travel dates: Your first international flight must depart on or before 11 December 2026, between 1 January and 12 March 2027, or between 11 April and 20 June 2027
Minimum stay at the destination of six days, or until the first Sunday after you arrive
Maximum stay at the destination of three months
Stopovers permitted in China – one in each direction at EUR100 (~AU$167) each, for up to 14 days
Change fee: EUR450 (~AU$751), plus any difference in fare
Cancellation fee: EUR850 (~AU$1,418)
No-show fee: EUR950 (~AU$1,585), charged on top of any change or cancellation fee if you don’t change or cancel at least 30 minutes before departure
On-board product
China Southern uses its Boeing 787-9 aircraft between Madrid and Guangzhou. While China Southern has three layout variations of this type, over the last month all aircraft operating this route have featured lie-flat seats in Business Class.
China Southern 787 at Sydney Airport. Photo: Matt Graham.
Flights between Guangzhou and Brisbane use either the Airbus A350 or Airbus A330 aircraft. All of China Southern’s A350s and most of its A330s feature lie-flat Business Class seats in a staggered 1-2-1 layout with direct aisle access. There is a small Airbus A330 sub-fleet that has an older 2-2-2 layout. Check the seat map before booking!
Earning points & status credits with this airfare
This fare books into “I” class. While China Southern isn’t part of any alliance, it has direct partnerships with a handful of airlines. You could earn redeemable points for this airfare in programs including:
American Airlines AAdvantage
British Airways Club (Avios)
For example, if you credited these flights to either program, you could earn around 21,700 redeemable miles. American Airlines AAdvantage program could be a good option as Qantas Business Class redemptions anywhere within Australia cost just 20,000 miles one-way, and the taxes are very low.
Neither program awards status-qualifying credit on flights operated and marketed by China Southern. So if you’re chasing status, this isn’t the ticket for you.
